**A duplicate can be rejected before it reaches the vendor.** The shared export service validates documents before calling the provider adapter. If every document is rejected, it returns the rejection list immediately; in a mixed batch, only accepted documents proceed.

The duplicate checks are:

| Refusal reason | When it applies |
|---|---|
| `already_sent` | A matching provider document has upload status `uploaded`, processing status other than `archived`, and the **same return type**. |
| `upload_in_progress` | A matching provider document has upload status `waiting` or `uploading`. This check applies **across return types**. |

Both checks match the **firm, client, contact, tax year, provider, and document ID**. `already_sent` takes precedence over `upload_in_progress`.

Consequently:

- An archived upload no longer blocks resending through `already_sent`.
- An uploaded document under another return type does not trigger `already_sent`.
- A waiting/uploading document can still block that other-return-type send.
- Other upload statuses are not blocked by these two checks, though other validation can reject them.

Unsupported return type or tax year takes precedence over these duplicate reasons. File format and size checks follow them.

There is also a separate whole-request refusal for business returns: an EIN associated with an existing send under another client in the same firm produces an `unprocessable` error with `bound_account_id`, before document validation.

Sources: [document validation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export/validate_documents.rb:38), [early return before provider dispatch](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:53), [EIN guard](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:111).
